newsitem.title: USA: Arkansas wheat harvest, soy plantings slow on rain.
newsitem.headline: Arkansas wheat harvest, soy plantings slow on rain.

text.p: Heavy rains and flooding slowed soybean plantings and wheat harvest in Arkansas during the week ended Sunday, acccording to the state's weekly Agricultural Statistics Service update.
"Stormy conditions the first part of last week produced over five inches of rain in southwest Arkansas, causing flooding," the report said.

Soybeans were 76 percent planted, up slightly from 72 percent a week ago, but down from 82 percent a year ago and the 80 percent fiv- year average. Sixty-eight percent had emerged, versus an average 63 percent.
Soil moisture supplies were 15 percent very short, 55 percent adequate and 30 percent surplus.
Thirty-seven percent of soft red winter wheat was harvested, down from 67 percent a year ago and the 65 five-year average.
Rice was 100 percent emerged, which is equal to last year and just above the five-year average of 99 percent.
